svg.title: Obesity management by body mass index: lifestyle and psychology for everyone; a drug (tirzepatide or semaglutide first, naltrexone-bupropion next) at BMI 30, or 27 with complications; bariatric surgery at BMI 40, 35 with a complication, or 30 with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; each column gives what to check before, what to give, and what to expect or watch

svg.text: Obesity: how far up the ladder? BMI + complications decide

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30, or ≥ 25 South or East Asian · always with waist circumference

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: ASK permission first · ASSESS the 4 M's (mental, mechanical, metabolic, monetary)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: rule out hypothyroidism, Cushing's, medications · A1c, lipids, thyroid-stimulating hormone, alanine aminotransferase

svg.text: BMI ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with complications: ADD A DRUG

svg.text: ≥ 5% loss by 12 weeks at the maximum tolerated dose, else switch · likely
